input.quote: In addition, in the event that Array terminates this Agreement for Ono's breach pursuant to Section 13.3 during the [ * ], or Ono exercises its right to terminate this Agreement "at will" pursuant to Section 13.2 during the Initial Royalty Term, then neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize a Competing Product or grant the right to a licensee or distributor to Commercialize a Competing Product in the Ono Territory prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 ("Exclusivity of Efforts") binds Ono not to Commercialize a "Competing Product" (products containing a MEK- or BRAF-type inhibitor other than Binimetinib/Encorafenib) in the Ono Territory. The first sentence is a mutual, during-term, product-class-limited restriction that also binds Array in our territory, so that part sits within the bargain and benefits us as well. The second sentence, however, is a post-termination non-compete on Ono only, running to an unspecified ("[ * ]") anniversary of termination and triggered even where Ono terminates at will — this fails the fallback (restriction "during the term only, capped at 12 months") and falls into walk-away territory for a post-term tail exceeding 12 months. We therefore propose deleting the post-term tail to reach the preferred position, noting in the comment that a 12-month tail with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs would be an acceptable fallback. We also note the restriction covers a compound class rather than a single named product and lacks express development/acquisition carve-outs, but as it is limited to Commercialization in the Ono Territory and is reciprocal during the term, we raise those only as observations.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the post-termination restriction on Ono commercialising a Competing Product, as we cannot accept a non-compete that survives termination (including where we terminate at will) for an unspecified period. We are comfortable with the mutual during-term exclusivity in the first sentence; if Array needs post-term protection, we could accept a tail of no more than twelve (12) months with carve-outs for internal development and acquired programs.
proposal.summary: Delete the post-termination non-compete tail binding Ono in Section 8.2, leaving the mutual during-term exclusivity intact.
